governance.constitution:

- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.

findings.description: The plan guards only concurrent duplicate onboarding prompts, not coexistence with another Refine modal. Bootstrap calls navigate before the delayed Reporter refresh; Goal detail, Feature detail/new, and Import routes can therefore already have a modal open when onboarding starts. These dialogs use document-level Escape/Enter handlers, so stacking can close or submit more than one dialog and breaks a single accessible focus context.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit modal-coordination contract: defer onboarding while any other modal is active (or use a shared top-dialog manager), then re-check attached project and selected Reporter before opening. Specify labeled dialog controls, initial focus, focus containment/restoration, and topmost-only Escape/backdrop behavior. Test cold deep links to existing modal routes and prove only one dialog handles keyboard input.

findings.description: P2 invokes onboarding only after the one startup refreshReporters call succeeds, while init.js intentionally swallows an initial Reporter hydration failure. The existing SSE reporters_changed and project_updated paths can later hydrate Reporters, but the plan does not reconnect those successful refreshes to onboarding. A transient initial failure can therefore leave the user indefinitely unprompted with an empty, potentially unusable Controls selector until reload.
findings.recommendation: Make onboarding eligibility safely re-invocable after every relevant successful Reporter hydration, without polling, while retaining the open/in-flight guard and re-checking project/selection state. Add a deterministic test for initial GET failure followed by successful hydration and exactly one prompt.

findings.description: The plan and its evidence require POST /api/reporters followed by refreshReporters and only then setLastReporter. POST already returns the durably created Reporter, and FileReporterService creation is idempotent. If POST succeeds but the follow-up GET fails, that ordering leaves selection empty and presents a retryable creation failure even though durable state changed.
findings.recommendation: Treat creation and refresh as separate outcomes: after a successful POST, select the returned canonical Reporter immediately, close or advance onboarding, and attempt list refresh independently. If refresh fails, retain the valid selection and report only that the Reporter list refresh failed. Test POST success plus GET failure, persisted selection, and later reconciliation.

result.summary: Retain the focused Reporter-onboarding module and thin startup hook, but revise the plan before implementation to coordinate with existing dialogs, make later successful Reporter hydration re-trigger the onboarding eligibility check, and preserve a Reporter that was durably created even if the follow-up list refresh fails. Extend deterministic and browser coverage for those recovery and interaction contracts.

findings.description: P2 explicitly calls setLastReporter before closing or advancing onboarding. In current main, setLastReporter calls navigate when the first Reporter is selected on goals_new, goals_import, or goals_detail. That allows route rendering and modal lifecycle work to begin while onboarding still owns its document key handler, focus trap, backdrop, and restoration target, undermining P1's no-stacking/topmost-only contract. The plan also does not distinguish a successful close from yielding to an asynchronously arriving blocker; restoring connected prior focus during a yield can steal focus from the new top dialog.
findings.recommendation: Define a reason-aware settlement order. On successful existing selection or POST creation, first retire onboarding and its observer/listeners without restoring focus into the underlay, then synchronously update the in-memory canonical Reporter and call setLastReporter, and only then perform GET reconciliation. On blocker yield, remove onboarding without ordinary dismissal state or focus restoration and let the blocker retain focus. Add a real goals/new or goals/import route test and an asynchronous Feature-detail blocker test proving one aria-modal dialog, one Escape/Enter consumer, and focus remaining in the top dialog throughout.

findings.description: The plan evaluates eligibility only after refreshReporters reconciles selection, but current main's applyProjectAttachResult calls refreshNodeScopedState({ selectReporterFallback: true }). reconcileLastReporter then silently calls setLastReporter with the first Reporter. The resulting attached UI appears to have a valid selection and suppresses onboarding even though the user never identified themselves, contrary to the stated no-valid-selected-Reporter contract and browser-local user choice authority.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly resolve the fallback interaction in P2: remove first-Reporter fallback from the attach path (or otherwise preserve the pre-reconciliation absence as onboarding eligibility without persisting an arbitrary identity). Add deterministic coverage for attaching or switching to a project with multiple Reporters and no stored valid selection, proving no Reporter is silently persisted and exactly one onboarding dialog is offered.

findings.description: The idempotent hydration trigger has no specified terminal state for an intentional dismissal. Because selection remains empty, every later successful reporters_changed, project_updated, or feature-triggered refresh can reopen the dialog, which is not a gentle dismissal and makes 'dismissal/retry' nondeterministic. The plan also specifies only POST success; it does not say how POST rejection retains the entered name, reenables submission, exposes an accessible error, and permits a safe retry without creating duplicate prompts or changing selection.
findings.recommendation: Separate deferred, dismissed, submitting, failed, and completed outcomes. Define a page-lifetime dismissal latch that suppresses automatic hydration reopen while leaving Controls > Reporter as the explicit retry path (or state another precise retry policy), without treating the latch as identity persistence. For POST failure, keep the same dialog and draft open, restore enabled controls/focus, announce an inline role=alert or live-region error, and leave state/localStorage unchanged. Test repeated hydrations after dismissal, explicit retry, POST rejection followed by success, single-request behavior, preserved input, and accessible error announcement.

result.summary: The revised plan substantially addresses the three Round 1 criticisms, but it is not yet safe to implement as written. It finalizes Reporter selection before retiring onboarding even though setLastReporter can synchronously re-enter modal routes; it does not account for the existing project-attach fallback that silently chooses the first Reporter before eligibility is evaluated; and it leaves dismissal plus POST-failure retry behavior undefined under a deliberately repeatable hydration trigger. These gaps can still produce competing modal lifecycles, bypass onboarding, or turn a gentle prompt into repeated reopening.

checklist.description: Make refreshReporters' successful state update, selection reconciliation, and dropdown population the single thin notification point for onboarding eligibility, so startup, reporters_changed, project_updated, settings, import, and feature/Goal refresh callers all reach the same idempotent controller path. Ensure attached project_updated events hydrate Reporters through that path on every route, allowing a failed initial GET to recover through a later SSE or project update without polling. Remove selectReporterFallback from applyProjectAttachResult, refreshNodeScopedState, and reconcileLastReporter so attaching or switching projects clears invalid prior selection but never persists the first Reporter as an invented identity; valid browser-local selections on ordinary startup remain selected. For an existing choice, first settle onboarding as completed and synchronously remove its DOM, focus trap, key listener, and modal observer without restoring underlay focus, then call setLastReporter so any resulting navigate() may safely open goals/new, goals/import, or goals/detail.
